### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 329121397b395e688cff1ca9e845e07ba53c652a`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 329121397b395e688cff1ca9e845e07ba53c652a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2909be5b7511cdc2ee94fd20fd08c2f629cd8fc4` — the merge of head `ee0e30c96c3c8aba7fbb570fd5e9b00e58a80ccb` into base `329121397b395e688cff1ca9e845e07ba53c652a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2909be5b7511cdc2ee94fd20fd08c2f629cd8fc4 && git checkout 2909be5b7511cdc2ee94fd20fd08c2f629cd8fc4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 329121397b395e688cff1ca9e845e07ba53c652a ee0e30c96c3c8aba7fbb570fd5e9b00e58a80ccb && git checkout -B drift-repro 329121397b395e688cff1ca9e845e07ba53c652a && git merge --no-ff ee0e30c96c3c8aba7fbb570fd5e9b00e58a80ccb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 329121397b395e688cff1ca9e845e07ba53c652a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 329121397b395e688cff1ca9e845e07ba53c652a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`GET /meta/_drafts` with any query key that opens `packageId[` or `type[` (`?packageId[]=ID`, `?packageId[0]=ID`, `?type[]=TYPE`, `?type[0]=TYPE`, `?packageId[id]=`, `?type[name]=`): 200 with every draft the caller may read becomes 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, no list, on both transports, before any binding.** Right. The dogfood control pins that a member is still refused 403 at the capability gate before the bracketed key is judged.

The retired body built `listFilterRefusalMessage(key, 'package', "the 'package' filter takes exactly one package id, spelled ?package=ID", "a bracketed 'package' key", tree ? 'tree' : 'list', tree ? 'read the tree across every package' : 'list across every package')`. []` returns `undefined` there, where the retired body's `includes('package')` did). `bracketedKeyOf` matches `startsWith('param[')`, so `types[`, `packageIds[`, `package[` on `_drafts` and `packageId[` / `type[` on the list and the tree stay unread (pinned as data). `?packageId=ID` and `?type=TYPE` still narrow, absent ones list every draft (pinned on `RestServer` with the exact `listDrafts` arguments, on the dispatcher, and over HTTP with the rows asserted to match). The `/meta/:type` list, the book tree, `state`, every by-name door, `/data` and every non-`/meta` door are untouched.
6. **Public surface.** `metaBracketedPackageRefusal` was never on `packages/rest/src/index.ts` (the entry exports `metaQueryArityRefusal`, `metaItemQueryRefusal`, `META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS` and their siblings from `meta-item-read-gate.js`, not the bracket helper), the package's `exports` map has the one `.` entry, and `git grep metaBracketedPackageRefusal` over the whole head tree returns nothing, so the rename is a module-internal move with no consumer, not a published-surface break. `metaBracketedFilterRefusal` is likewise not exported from the entry. `MetaItemQueryRefusal.rule` is the same four-member union on the head as on the merge-base; no new export, error code, status, answer member or wire field. `check-platform-checklist` reported 12 anchors judged, 0 lost (the dev's reading; `Lint · repo & tooling gates` is green on this head).

The narrowing, read against the published contract on `main`: `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` declares `GET /meta/_drafts` by its response only (`ListDraftsResponseSchema`, 2265-2300); the request's two filters are declared where they are consumed, as one optional string each (`@objectstack/client`'s `listDrafts(opts?: { packageId?: string; type?: string })` and the kernel's `listDrafts({ packageId, type })` argument both transports build), and `META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS.drafts` already names each as single-valued (#23214: a repeat is refused).
